common_name: Red Beard Bunching Onion (Red-Tinted Cold-Hardy Scallion)

planting.note: Direct sow or start transplants in early spring; can also be sown in late summer for a fall crop in zone 9. Red Beard develops its reddish shank color best in cool weather with full sun.

directions: Sow seed a quarter inch deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, thinning to about an inch apart for straight, uniform stalks. Red Beard is a non-bulbing bunching onion selected for shanks that develop an attractive reddish-pink blush, especially in cool weather, adding color contrast to salads, garnishes, and stir-fries beyond standard all-green scallions. It is cold-hardy and can be sown in late summer for a fall and winter harvest in mild climates, standing in the garden through cool weather without bolting. Harvest at scallion size for the best color and tenderness, or let a portion mature further for thicker stalks; successive small sowings every few weeks keep a continuous supply through the cool season.
sources: University of Minnesota Extension — Growing Onions
